title: N0 with the active-torque target: subtract the clean passive table (static relaxed holds) instead of predicting total torque.
hypothesis: Same as N0 except the target. Run to see whether the 10 s calibration also works when the target is active torque.
motivation: Calibration follow-up (2 Nov 2026): 0.2 s window, balanced positions, session-1 maximum scaling, no auto-gain, LSTM 8x2, 6 people, seeds 0-2, session 1 -> session 2.

dashboard.label: Balanced positions · active torque
dashboard.name: Balanced positions (predicts active torque)

text.purpose: Exactly N0 (session-1 maximum, balanced positions, 0.2 s), but the network learns active torque: total torque minus the clean passive table built from the relaxed holds of each session (IES has no holds, so the old passive rule is used for IES).
text.target: Active torque: total measured torque minus the clean passive table of that session (relaxed holds). Scored against active torque.
text.protocol: Train on session 1, test on session 2. Active torque, 0.2 s window (20 samples at 100 Hz) of four muscle envelopes plus angle. Balanced positions (each position’s target ÷ its standard deviation). LSTM 8×2, dropout 0.3, batch 8, at most 200 epochs, early stopping after 25. People: CH, EG, HM, IES, JM, YES. Seeds: 0, 1, 2.

settings: Session 1 → session 2 · 8 angles · one ~90 s trial per angle
4 EMG envelopes (GM, GL, SOL, TA) + ankle angle, 100 Hz
0.2 s = 20 samples → torque at the window’s last sample
Active torque: total minus that session’s clean passive table (relaxed holds)
Yes: each position’s target ÷ its standard deviation
steps: EMG: band-pass 30–300 Hz, rectify, 2 Hz low-pass → envelope (1 kHz), then down-sampled to 100 Hz.
Scale: Each muscle envelope is divided by the largest value it reached anywhere in session 1 (one sample of the 1 kHz envelope). Session 2 is divided by the same four numbers.
Standardise the 5 inputs (mean 0, sd 1) with session 1’s training statistics.
Cut 0.2 s windows sliding by one sample. Each session-1 trial: first 80 % to fit, last 20 % to stop training.
Train the LSTM on the target ÷ each position’s standard deviation, then multiply its predictions back (Nadam, lr 0.003, batch 8, ≤ 200 epochs, early stopping after 25).
Predict every window of session 2, which the model never saw.
Score each position on every 100 Hz sample: R² = 1 − Σ(y − ŷ)² / Σ(y − ȳ)², MAE = mean |y − ŷ|. Median over seeds, then median across positions; R² below 0 is shown as 0.

dashboard.blurb: Balanced positions; the network predicts active torque, with each session’s relaxed-hold passive torque subtracted.
